I will keep the whole 8 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation. That is what my land knows, and I do not want to take a big risk at my age. Wheat gives us steady grain, and after wheat I put in maize right away so the land does not stay empty. I mostly do what has worked on my own fields and what people around me do. Last year when the wheat looked a bit weak, the extra topdressing helped, so this year I will still feed the wheat a bit heavier than the maize. Money matters, because some people in the family work outside and cash is never loose, so I will not buy the most expensive seed or too much fertilizer all at once.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, using a common local improved seed that is easy to buy in the market. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then watch the seedlings and give another round around jointing if the leaves are pale. Since we have well water, I will irrigate wheat about 3 times if the weather is normal: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once around overwintering or greening, and once around jointing or grain filling. Wheat is the crop I do not dare starve too much. After harvest in June, I will hurry to plant summer maize on all 8 mu within a few days. That turnaround is always tight, so I will do simple rotary tillage or direct planting with hired machine help if needed. Maize I will manage a bit more simply: one base fertilizer round and one topdress around knee-high stage, and irrigate 1 or 2 times depending on rain. If pests show up, I spray; if not, I do not waste money.
